gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured brightness, contrast or colour figure for any laptop screen extender. The closest is Notebookcheck's meter test of a FOPO 12-inch triple extender (two added screens), which measured 185 cd/m² at the centre, 247:1 contrast and 79% sRGB.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Apple Support 117373, the cited DisplayLink Manager First Time Configuration page and Macworld's multi-monitor guide (updated 2026-11-19, a top result). Apple gives only display counts and resolutions. DisplayLink gives only setup and permission steps. Macworld gives DisplayLink's 60 Hz cap and says it 'may introduce noticeable latency', with no figure. None of the three measures any extender's screen. The finding is new but it is a proxy: Notebookcheck tested a 2022 FOPO 12-inch model, not one we link, and tested it on an HP laptop, not a Mac.
decides: The finding confirms the pick but does not change it. On an M3 MacBook Air with the lid open, Apple's page supports only one external display, and a second external display goes dark. So a single added screen over native USB-C (e.g. Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS) is the driver-free answer. Two-screen extenders need a display driver: DisplayLink, Mobile Pixels' own driver or FOPO's UsbDisplay. The measurements add a buyer expectation. Notebookcheck's meter read a FOPO extender panel at 185 cd/m² centre and 247:1. Macworld (Simon Jary) found that the Trio 3 Pro's 300-nit screens cannot reach full brightness on laptop power alone. Budget for a power adapter if brightness matters.
